**Finding: compliant (preferred level) — no redline proposed.**

§22 (Audit Rights) is the only provision in the agreement creating audit, inspection or verification rights against us, and it satisfies all eight preferred elements:

| Preferred element | Where met |
|---|---|
| Once per 12 months | §22.1 "no more than once in any twelve-month period" |
| 30 days' written notice | §22.1 "at least thirty days' prior written notice" |
| Business hours | §22.1 "during normal business hours" |
| Independent auditor | §22.1 "by an independent auditor" |
| Auditor confidentiality | §22.1 "bound by confidentiality" |
| Off-site where possible | §22.1 "off-site where practicable" |
| Vendor cost unless >5% underpayment | §22.2 "unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent" |
| No direct system access | §22.2 "Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly" |

Investigation notes across the full document:
- **§23 "Records and Customer Assurance"** is a bare heading with no operative text — it imposes no record-keeping or self-certification duty that could function as a back-door audit.
- **No other clause** uses audit/inspection/verification/monitoring language against us; the only "usage" reference (§7) concerns usage-based unit pricing, and §26.4 requires *Vendor* to follow our policies when accessing our systems (a benefit to us).
- **§2.3** blocks website, click-through, invoice, quotation and support-portal terms from applying, so no external document can import broader audit rights; §2.2's precedence order does not subordinate §22 to any vendor-supplied exhibit on audits.
- **§22.3** adds further customer-favourable protections (audit findings are our Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of the final report, shortfall payment resolves the issue absent fraud), which we would not disturb.

No walk-away features (unlimited or unannounced audits, remote system access) exist. The clause sits at preferred, not merely fallback, so no change is warranted.
